scoringCalibration: The front hairline is materially cleaner: detached forehead fibers and cards are removed and the baby-hair transition is shorter and irregular. No point is awarded because ear-side grouping, the rear nape edge, crown breakup and engine hair shading still fail the same production-quality gate.
visualFindings: Long isolated fibers and broad cards no longer cross the forehead or approach the brows in front and three-quarter views.
The baby-hair transition uses sparse clustered placement, varied direction and shorter tapered ribbons instead of an evenly spaced comb pattern.
Side and rear inspection still exposes regular temple strokes and a straight nape curtain, so the groom remains below review quality.
rejectedExperiments: The first v43 candidate used a 2 mm exclusion below the hairline and 126 nearly stratified baby hairs; it was rejected because several detached forehead cards and a comb rhythm remained.
Awarding a hair-quality point for the cleaner front was rejected because the side and rear silhouette still fails the existing production gate.
blockingFailures: The groom still needs hand-shaped crown breakup, deliberate ear-side groups and a natural staggered nape edge.
Hair shading still needs an engine-side dual-lobe anisotropic model and strand-scale roughness variation.
The body needs expression-compatible lip loops and a deformable mouth opening before teeth and tongue can be exposed during speech.
Integrated upper and lower eyelid thickness and expression-compatible canthus topology remain below review quality.
Clothing edge flow, seams, folds, materials and outer layers remain below review quality.
Raised-arm shoulders still require corrective deformation and the standard pose suite remains incomplete.
Signed clothing-distance samples remain negative despite zero exact triangle overlaps in the audited frames.
LOD transition popping and frame-time impact remain untested in the website renderer.
